title: AuditLogViewer
wrapsNative: NavigationStack with MonarchCursorList rows (Buttons), searchable(text:prompt:), safeAreaInset(edge: .top) with MonarchTag filter chips (the filter-bar recipe), a toolbar ShareLink for export, and sheet(item:) with presentationDetents([.medium, .large]) holding a List of LabeledContent (the log-drawer recipe) with a relative time
summary: A recipe, not a component: security and audit events (who did what, to what, from where and when) as a searchable, filterable list that loads more, with a detail sheet for each event and an export.
whenToUse: In workspace or product settings, an audit log for admins and security reviews: sign-ins, key use, permission changes and exports.
whenNotToUse: For a record's own history in context use MonarchActivityTimeline. For an API request log use the log-drawer recipe with MonarchDataTable or a List. Audit entries are read-only; do not offer editing.
api: NavigationStack { MonarchCursorList(events, label: "Audit events", hasMore:, isLoading:, onLoadMore: { … }, row: { event in Button { selected = event } label: { … } }).searchable(text: $query, prompt: "Search events").safeAreaInset(edge: .top) { MonarchTag(…, isSelected: $filter) }.navigationTitle("Audit log").toolbar { ShareLink(item: csv) { … } }.sheet(item: $selected) { event in NavigationStack { List { LabeledContent("Actor") { … } … Section("Changes") { … } }.navigationTitle("Event details") }.presentationDetents([.medium, .large]) } }

options.name: events
options.description: One row per event, newest first: the sentence "actor action target" and, muted, the actor kind and the absolute time. hasMore, isLoading and onLoadMore page through the log with the service's cursor.

options.name: search
options.description: The system search field in the navigation bar; the app filters on the server for large logs.

options.name: filters
options.description: Quick filters such as actor kind or action in the top safe-area inset; more filters in a sheet, as in the filter-bar recipe.

options.name: export
options.description: Shares the loaded events as CSV; export everything on the server for large logs.

options.name: details
options.description: The full record of an event: actor and its kind, action, target, origin (IP and device), the time as relative with the absolute time spoken, and the before and after of a change.

states.name: ready
states.description: The rows, newest first, with Load more while there are more.

states.name: failed
states.description: MonarchCursorList shows its error with Try again (onRetry).

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchCursorList's end text, or a MonarchEmptyState of the filtered kind with Clear filters when filters hide everything.

states.name: no access
states.description: Replace the list with MonarchEmptyState explaining who can see the audit log.

states.name: details open
states.description: A sheet at medium height that can be pulled to large, with Close in the confirmation slot.

appearance: System navigation bar, search field and sheet; rows use the default text colour for the sentence and the muted text colour for kind and time; the actor kind in the sheet is a neutral MonarchBadge. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web ships AuditLogViewer as one component: a table with time, actor, action, target and origin columns, a density option, column choice, a side drawer, filters, export and paging. On a phone a multi-column table does not fit, so each event is a list row written as a sentence with its kind and time, and the drawer is a sheet with detents (the log-drawer recipe). Columns and density have no meaning in a list. The web's auditLogToCsv helper is the app's: the recipe shares a simple CSV with ShareLink, and large exports belong on the server. Absolute times in the list and a relative time in the details follow the web; in tests and screenshots give the relative formatter a fixed reference time. Actor kinds are text, never colour alone. Android has the same recipe coverage and status (available).
accessibility: Each row is one button read as the sentence, then the actor kind and the time, with the hint "Shows the event details".
Rows are at least 44 points high.
MonarchCursorList announces new pages and its end, and Load more is a standard button.
In the sheet each fact is one element read as the term and the value; the relative time is spoken as the full date and time.
People, automations, systems and API keys are told apart by text in a badge, not by colour.
Close is in the standard place, and the escape gesture closes the sheet.
edgeCases: Leave out facts an event does not have, such as the before and after of an export.
Long targets and origins wrap; IP addresses and ids stay on one line where they fit.
Deep links to an event set selected to open its sheet.
At the largest text sizes the rows grow taller and the sheet content scrolls.
